stem: Naveen compares copper, steel, and shiny coal for drawing into thin wires for a lamp cord. Which claim is correct?

options.text: Copper can be drawn into wires because it is ductile.
Copper can be drawn into wires because it is malleable.
Steel cannot be drawn into wires because it contains carbon.
Shiny coal can be drawn into wires.

teacher.key_rationale: Wire-drawing needs ductility. Copper is ductile. Malleability is for sheets, not wires. Steel can still be drawn into wires. Coal is not ductile even when shiny.
